data.title: Create a bounded background crowd
data.summary: Three licensed animated characters, twelve positions and three phase offsets. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: InstancedMesh shares geometry/materials across multiple world transforms.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender animation / engine clips environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: Three licensed animated characters, twelve positions and three phase offsets.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent crowd variation workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: Three licensed animated characters, twelve positions and three phase offsets. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Reuse source meshes and clips rather than creating twelve unique rigs
Assign clip phase and scale from an explicit placement table
Profile the actual crowd implementation; use a supported instancing or crowd system only where available

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned create a bounded background crowd candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: Each character has a valid clip reference
Animation memory and draw calls are measured in the complete scene
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: Crowd animation support and skinning costs vary between runtimes.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Static InstancedMesh is not a drop-in solution for arbitrary skinned characters.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me create a bounded background crowd in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: Three licensed animated characters, twelve positions and three phase offsets. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: Each character has a valid clip reference; Animation memory and draw calls are measured in the complete scene. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
